policy_chain: The prior inspected app_neverallows.te5-18 includes untrusted_app_all in all_untrusted_apps; line111 neverallows file_type:file link.
seapp_contexts225-226 selects runas_app for fromRunAs; runas.te30-33 grants the transition to app security context, not a general file-link capability before executing arbitrary user commands.
conclusion: The ordinary existing run-as app domain is covered by the same AOSP hardlink neverallow, not a platform-valid Enforcing workaround for fixture provisioning. Matching UID/label and debuggable status do not remove that type-enforcement rule. No run-as retry or harness change is justified by these sources.
preexisting_alias_limit: Pre-existing externally provisioned hardlinks may still be a valid defensive library scenario. This review does not prove that all such inputs are impossible, waive native hardlink acceptance, or replace it with host/symlink/bind/provider evidence. Trusted external provisioning would be a separately authorized, provenance-controlled harness design, not the current ordinary run-as route.
limitations: Public android-15.0.0_r1 policy source, not an exact compiled-policy extraction from emulator002 or the earlier image.
The lead is running42 unchanged IO/picker cases. No source edit, runtime input, device policy, historical test ID or skip policy changed here.
